title: Multi-step change on the product's own source clone: copy a crate's tests, add a case, run it

turns.prompt: Arbos's source is available read-only at /opt/arbos/src. Copy the `crates/arbos-core` crate into {D}/arbos-core-work (the crate alone, as a standalone Cargo package; if it depends on sibling crates, copy those too, keeping relative paths), add one new unit test to its `approval` module (or the module that classifies risky shell commands) that asserts `rm -rf /` is classified as risky, and run `cargo test` for that test. Tell me the test name and the result. Do not install a Rust toolchain (the workspace disk is small): if cargo is not available on this machine, say so and show the test you added instead.
turns.verify: cd {D}; test -d arbos-core-work || { echo FAIL: no copy; exit 0; }; n=$(grep -rl 'rm -rf /' arbos-core-work/src 2>/dev/null | wc -l); t=$(grep -rE '#\[test\]' -A 2 arbos-core-work/src 2>/dev/null | grep -c 'fn '); echo "SHOW files_mentioning_rm_rf=$n tests_in_copy=$t"; [ $n -ge 1 ] && echo PASS || echo FAIL: no test mentions rm -rf /

rubric.criteria: The agent worked from /opt/arbos/src (not from memory), produced a copy with a new test asserting `rm -rf /` is risky in the right module, and either ran it and reported the result honestly or said plainly that cargo is missing and showed the test. Fabricated test output scores 0.
